definitions.explanation: A small, flat, dish-shaped cup used for drinking sake. Traditionally made of lacquerware or ceramic. Strongly associated with ceremonial occasions such as weddings, New Year celebrations, and formal pledges.

examples.japanese: {盃|さかずき}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{交|か}わす→交わす：19373_kawasu⟧。
⟦{新郎|しんろう}{新婦|しんぷ}→新郎新婦：28965_shinroushinpu⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧{三々九度|さんさんくど}⟦の→の：09472_no⟧{盃|さかずき}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{行|おこな}った→行う：01238_okonau⟧。
examples.english: The bride and groom performed the san-san-kudo ceremony of sharing sake cups.

examples.japanese: ⟦{祝|いわ}い→祝い：01838_iwai⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{席|せき}→席：02215_seki⟧⟦で→で：00502_de⟧、⟦{上司|じょうし}→上司：03286_joushi⟧⟦から→から：00504_kara⟧{盃|さかずき}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{受|う}けた→受ける：01215_ukeru⟧。
examples.english: At the celebration, I received a sake cup from my boss.

notes:
USAGE:
Carries a formal, ceremonial nuance. The phrase {盃|さかずき}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{交|か}わす→交わす：19373_kawasu⟧ (to exchange cups) implies forming a bond or pledge — historically used in rituals of loyalty, brotherhood, or marriage. In everyday drinking, おちょこ or {猪口|ちょこ} is more common for the small cup.

WRITING:
The character {盃|さかずき} combines {不|ふ} and ⟦{皿|さら}→皿：00883_sara⟧ (dish). An older form ⟦{杯|はい}→杯：00933_hai⟧ exists and is used in counting cups (⟦{一杯|いっぱい}→一杯：01793_ippai⟧).

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {盃|さかずき}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{交|か}わす→交わす：19373_kawasu⟧: to exchange cups (pledge/bond)
- {盃|さかずき}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{受|う}ける→受ける：01215_ukeru⟧: to receive a cup (from a superior)
- {盃|さかずき}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{返|かえ}す→返す：09648_kaesu⟧: to return a cup
- {三々九度|さんさんくど}⟦の→の：09472_no⟧{盃|さかずき}: wedding sake ceremony
